label: copy phase, re-reading a/c/d mid-copy
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (never on original or delimiter steps, never at recall_idx 0-1), mostly at t=10-13 / recall_idx 3-5 of longer sequences (L=8-9 hold ~70% of mass). Strongly selective for the fed-back input token: a (53% of mass, 15x lift), then d and c; f/s/0/y/q/n weakly; digits 1-3 and most letters essentially never. Only fires on repeat occurrences (in_first=0, trivially true in copy). The predicate captures ~80% of activation mass but precision is ~5%: most copy-phase a/c/d inputs do not activate it, and no simple token-history, position, or count condition tested (L, t window, prev_tok, out_count) separates active from inactive cases. Largest activations are on a/c/d at recall_idx 2-3. Magnitudes are tiny (max ~0.001), so the unit is near-threshold noise-like beyond the token selectivity.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=12: a, c, d, f; t=11: a, d, c, f; t=9: a, d, c, f) and the token being output (most: c, a, y, 0, d, q; least: t, z, o, 3); timing cues that raise it most: L=3 & t=5, recall_idx=3, L=4 & t=6.
